scenes.heading: Parquet Format
scenes.narration: Parquet is a binary, columnar storage format designed to make large-scale analytical queries fast and efficient.

scenes.heading: Why analytics loves Parquet
bullets: Stores data by column, not by row
Compresses far better than text formats
Lets queries read only the columns they need
Carries the schema inside the file
scenes.narration: Parquet stores data column by column, which groups similar values together. That layout compresses far better than row-based text formats, saving storage and bandwidth. It also lets a query read only the columns it needs, skipping the rest entirely. And because the schema is embedded in the file, the data stays self-describing.

scenes.heading: Row storage vs columnar storage
scenes.narration: Row-based formats like CSV must read entire rows even when a query needs one column. Columnar formats like Parquet read only the columns requested and compress each column tightly. That is precisely why analytical engines scan Parquet far faster than text formats.

scenes.heading: How a query benefits
scenes.narration: When a query asks for just a couple of columns, Parquet skips over all the others on disk. It then reads only the relevant, tightly compressed data. The result is dramatically less I/O and much faster query performance.

scenes.text: Parquet's columnar layout and compression make it the default format for analytical data at scale.
scenes.narration: In short, Parquet's columnar layout and strong compression make it the default storage format for analytical workloads.
